sectors.trend: Bifurcated: Broadcom defends targets, Nvidia projected to $400, but $33T in stock gains ride on AI future; Gundlach warns of overexposure; Google AI security breach reported
sectors.implications: AI remains primary market driver but valuation risk and concentration risk (interconnectedness) create vulnerability; selective positioning favored over broad exposure

sectors.trend: Oil prices dropping pre-summit; tanker rates soaring; Chevron CEO signals confidence; Citi flags oil as key market risk variable; gas prices near yearly highs
sectors.implications: Falling oil supports equities short-term but geopolitical supply risks (Black Sea, Pakistan-Afghanistan) create volatility; energy equities offer defensive yield

sectors.trend: Bank7 acquires Century Financial ($137.3M); Goldman flags Virgin Media bonds as buy; Visa/Mastercard $167.5M settlement; Turkey fund crisis; FX market modernizing
sectors.implications: Consolidation continues in banking; regulatory settlements create tail risk; emerging market fund stress (Turkey) warrants caution

sectors.trend: Dollar General CEO flags consumer weakness; business owners in crisis; Wendy's franchisee bankruptcy; Christmas retailer Chapter 11; but Toys 'R' Us opens 120 stores
sectors.implications: Consumer bifurcation: luxury/collector spending resilient, value/discount under pressure; recession risk for lower-income segments

sectors.trend: Bitcoin at $84K (8-month high); $300M shorts liquidated; XRP surging; regulatory progress; Polymarket fraud concerns
sectors.implications: Risk-on rotation into crypto; regulatory clarity supports adoption but fraud/operational risks persist

sectors.trend: India IPO boom (5.7x oversubscription); Dimon in India for deal flow; Chile attracts foreign capital; HKEX eases listing rules
sectors.implications: Capital rotation toward EM; India is primary beneficiary of global deal-making resurgence

sectors.trend: Novo Nordisk 2030 strategy disappoints, stock falls; private hospitals see higher volumes
sectors.implications: GLP-1 competition intensifying; long-term growth intact but near-term execution risk

risk_assessment.mitigation: Maintain hedged positions; avoid directional bets pre-summit; use options for asymmetric payoff
Cap AI sector at 15-20% portfolio; diversify into non-AI tech; monitor Broadcom/Nvidia guidance vs. actuals
Overweight defensives (staples, utilities); reduce discretionary exposure; monitor Dollar General, Wendy's as leading indicators
Limit EM exposure to India/Chile; avoid Turkey, Pakistan; hold gold as hedge
Ladder bond maturities; avoid locking in long-duration at current yields; monitor Goolsbee/FOMC commentary
Monitor regulatory policy shifts; avoid over-concentration in politically exposed sectors

risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge energy exposure; monitor tanker rates as leading indicator; Citi's framework suggests oil drives cross-asset correlations

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid Turkey-linked funds and Pakistan/Afghanistan exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Asset freezes, border strikes create binary downside with limited recovery timeline

defensive_moves.recommendation: Monitor housing/mortgage stress; avoid over-leveraged real estate
defensive_moves.rationale: Mortgage rates soaring, affordability crisis deepening; Crown Castle dividend cut signals REIT stress

market_outlook.short_term: Risk-on bias pre-summit with oil as swing factor. BTC momentum and India IPO strength support equities. Consumer stress and Turkey crisis cap upside. Expect 2-3% volatility range around summit outcome. Goolsbee's 'painless' comment suggests Fed holds, supporting yields at 4.1-4.4%.
market_outlook.long_term: AI remains structural growth engine but concentration risk demands diversification. India/EM capital rotation is multi-year trend. Consumer bifurcation (wealth effect vs. distress) creates sector rotation opportunities. Trade resolution with China could re-rate global supply chains. Housing affordability remains structural headwind for 12+ months.
